```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(CDSeq2)
```

# Overview

CDSeq2 estimates RNA fractions and individual-level cell-type expression
from bulk RNA counts and an annotated single-cell reference. Its optional
six-feature generalized additive model prioritizes gene-cell-type profiles
whose cross-donor expression is expected to be recovered more accurately.
Prioritization changes the retained set, not the underlying expression estimates.
It is not an association test or a guarantee of false discovery rate control.

This fully synthetic example uses independent training and validation donors.
The short chains demonstrate the interface; scientific analyses require
convergence diagnostics and appropriate chain lengths. The synthetic scorer
is a teaching example and should not be used for biological samples.

# Simulate reference and bulk counts

Rows represent genes. Bulk columns represent donors; reference columns
represent cells. Component counts have gene, cell type and donor dimensions.

```{r simulation}
# Entirely synthetic teaching data; no participant data are used.
simulate_tutorial <- function() {
  set.seed(20261015)
  genes <- sprintf('Gene_%03d', seq_len(240))
  types <- c('Excitatory neurons', 'Inhibitory neurons', 'Astrocytes')
  mu <- matrix(rgamma(720, shape=1.5), 240, 3, dimnames=list(genes, types))
  for(k in 1:3) mu[((k-1)*60+1):(k*60),k] <- mu[((k-1)*60+1):(k*60),k]*8
  mu <- sweep(mu,2,colSums(mu),'/')
  annotation <- rep(types,each=12)
  reference <- vapply(seq_along(annotation),function(j)
    as.numeric(rmultinom(1,4000,mu[,annotation[j]])),numeric(240))
  dimnames(reference) <- list(genes,sprintf('Reference_cell_%02d',1:36))
  reference_donors <- rep(sprintf('Reference_donor_%02d',1:6),6)
  reference_mean <- vapply(types,function(ct)rowSums(reference[,annotation==ct,drop=FALSE]),numeric(240))
  reference_mean <- sweep(reference_mean,2,colSums(reference_mean),'/')
  dimnames(reference_mean) <- list(genes,types)
  make_cohort <- function(label,n=20) {
    samples <- sprintf('%s_%02d',label,seq_len(n))
    phenotype <- as.numeric(scale(rnorm(n)))
    genotype <- rbinom(n,2,.35)
    counts <- array(0,c(240,3,n),list(genes,types,samples))
    theta <- matrix(rgamma(n*3,shape=4),n,3,dimnames=list(samples,types))
    theta <- theta/rowSums(theta)
    for(i in seq_len(n)) for(k in 1:3) {
      z <- log(mu[,k])+rnorm(240,0,runif(240,.1,.65))
      if(k==1) {z[1:8] <- z[1:8]+.4*phenotype[i];z[9:16] <- z[9:16]+.45*(genotype[i]-.7)}
      counts[,k,i] <- as.numeric(rmultinom(1,round(30000*theta[i,k]),exp(z)))
    }
    list(bulk=apply(counts,c(1,3),sum),truth=counts,
      donor_ids=setNames(samples,samples),
      phenotype=setNames(phenotype,samples),genotype=setNames(genotype,samples))
  }
  list(reference=reference,annotation=annotation,reference_donors=reference_donors,
    reference_mean=reference_mean,training=make_cohort('Training'),validation=make_cohort('Validation'))
}
data <- simulate_tutorial()
```

# Infer expression and RNA fractions

```{r inference}
fit_tutorial <- function(cohort,data,seed) {
  fit <- CDSeq2::cdseq2(bulk_data=cohort$bulk,
    reference_scRNA_count=data$reference,
    reference_scRNA_annotation=data$annotation,
    reference_scRNA_donor=data$reference_donors,
    reference_aggregation='pooled_counts',reference_precision=10000,
    mcmc_iterations=100,save_last_n_mc=40,cpu_number=1,n_chains=1L,
    seed=seed,return_mcmc_arrays=FALSE,return_assignments=FALSE,verbose=FALSE)
  genes <- rownames(cohort$bulk);samples <- colnames(cohort$bulk)
  types <- colnames(data$reference_mean)
  # Paper-compatible posterior mean allocated reads, not estGEP_RB parameters.
  counts <- array(0,c(length(genes),length(types),length(samples)),list(genes,types,samples))
  fractions <- matrix(0,length(samples),length(types),dimnames=list(samples,types))
  for(i in seq_along(samples)) {
    counts[,,i] <- fit$cdseq_result[[i]]$estGEP_count
    fractions[i,] <- as.numeric(fit$cdseq_result[[i]]$estProp)
  }
  stopifnot(max(abs(apply(counts,c(1,3),sum)-cohort$bulk))<1e-6,
    max(abs(rowSums(fractions)-1))<1e-8)
  list(counts=counts,fractions=fractions,fit=fit)
}
training <- fit_tutorial(data$training, data, 101)
validation <- fit_tutorial(data$validation, data, 202)
head(validation$fractions)
```

# Train, validate and prioritize

Training requires known component expression. Applying a trained scorer requires
bulk counts, reference means and estimated fractions, but no truth. Donors used
for training must be distinct from validation and reference donors. Tissue,
cell-type coverage and inference settings should match the training context.

```{r prioritization}
make_tutorial_benchmark <- function(cohort,inferred,data,label) {
  CDSeq2::prepare_variation_benchmark(bulk=cohort$bulk,
    reference_mean=data$reference_mean,rna_fractions=inferred$fractions,
    estimated_counts=inferred$counts,truth_counts=cohort$truth,
    donor_ids=cohort$donor_ids,reference_donor_ids=unique(data$reference_donors),
    cohort_id=label,oracle='direct_observed_component_counts')
}
prioritize_tutorial <- function(data,training,validation) {
  train <- make_tutorial_benchmark(data$training,training,data,'synthetic_training')
  test <- make_tutorial_benchmark(data$validation,validation,data,'synthetic_validation')
  scorer <- CDSeq2::train_variation_scorer(train,context=list(
    application='Synthetic documentation tutorial',tissue='Synthetic brain-like mixture',
    deconvolution_method='CDSeq2',fit_settings=list(mcmc_iterations=100,
      save_last_n_mc=40,reference_precision=10000,estimator='estGEP_count + estProp')),
    folds=3L,min_profiles=50L,seed=20261015,model='GAM6')
  evaluation <- CDSeq2::validate_variation_scorer(scorer,test)
  features <- CDSeq2::prepare_variation_features(data$validation$bulk,
    data$reference_mean,validation$fractions,scorer=scorer)
  scores <- CDSeq2::score_variation(features,scorer,range_action='flag')
  selected <- CDSeq2::select_variation_profiles(scores,fraction=.2)
  stopifnot(all(table(selected$cell_type[selected$retained])==48),
    !any(data$training$donor_ids %in% data$validation$donor_ids),
    all(evaluation$donor_checks$training_target_overlap==0))
  list(scorer=scorer,evaluation=evaluation,selected=selected)
}
priority <- prioritize_tutorial(data, training, validation)
summary <- summarize_variation_selection(priority$selected)
summary
```

The selection fraction is applied within each supported cell type. Undefined
features and unsupported cell types are not silently assigned scores. Report
both recovery and coverage: retaining fewer profiles can improve precision
while reducing recall. Select retention thresholds independently of evaluation
truth. A scorer trained on one tissue or inference setting may not transfer.

# Save the trained model

```{r persistence}
model_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".rds")
save_variation_scorer(priority$scorer, model_file)
reloaded <- load_variation_scorer(model_file)
check_variation_scorer(reloaded)
unlink(model_file)
```

# Further resources

The [CDSeq2 book](https://kkang7.github.io/CDSeq2/) describes phenotype and eQTL
applications and reconstruction of the ROSMAP benchmarks. Full reproduction
materials and the frozen brain scorer are archived at
<https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23489824>. Large benchmark downloads are not
needed to run this vignette.
